results.question: What is a stack and what are the four main operations that can be performed on it?
results.expected_answer: A stack is a linear data structure that follows the Last In First Out (LIFO) principle. The four main operations are: Push (insert an element at the top), Pop (delete the top element), Peep (find the ith element from the top), and Change (update the value of the ith element from the top).

results.question: What is a linked list and what are its three main types?
results.expected_answer: A linked list is a linear data structure where each node contains data and a pointer to the next node. The three main types are: Singly Linked List (each node points to the next), Doubly Linked List (each node has pointers to both next and previous), and Circular Linked List (the last node points back to the first node).

results.question: What is a doubly linked list and how does it differ from a singly linked list?
results.expected_answer: A doubly linked list is a type of linked list where each node contains data and two pointers: one pointing to the next node and one pointing to the previous node. Unlike a singly linked list which only allows forward traversal, a doubly linked list allows traversal in both forward and reverse directions.

results.question: What is the role of the TOP pointer in a stack and what does it indicate when it is NULL or zero?
results.expected_answer: The TOP pointer points to the topmost element of the stack. When the stack is empty, TOP has a value of zero or NULL. It is incremented by one each time a new element is inserted (pushed) and decremented by one each time an element is deleted (popped).

results.question: What is stack underflow and when does it occur?
results.expected_answer: Stack underflow occurs when an attempt is made to delete (pop) an element from an empty stack. When TOP is NULL or zero, the stack is empty and a deletion attempt results in an UNDERFLOW condition or message.
